analysis.one_liner: Counts third-party payments and financial aid toward a patient's deductible and copays.
analysis.headline: The bill won House support from 62 cosponsors but never got a vote in the 117th Congress; it stalled in committee.
analysis.plain_summary: The HELP Copays Act would amend existing law to require health insurance plans to count payments made by third parties on behalf of the patient toward the patient's deductible, copay, and out-of-pocket limit. This closes a common gap where patients still end up paying more out of pocket even when a charity or family member paid on their behalf.
analysis.who_benefits: Insured patients who receive help paying their medical bills from charities, family, or nonprofits would save money because more of their healthcare costs would count toward reaching their deductible and out-of-pocket maximum faster.
analysis.who_benefits_short: Patients receiving third-party medical bill help

how_it_helps.text: Requires health plans to count payments made by or on behalf of the patient toward their deductible, coinsurance, copayments, and out-of-pocket limit.
Specifically covers third-party payments, financial assistance, discounts, product vouchers, and other reductions in out-of-pocket expenses.

analysis.who_pays: Health insurance companies would bear the cost, since they would have to cover more of the patient's share once third-party contributions count toward cost-sharing limits.

drawbacks.text: Insurers argue this could drive up premiums for all customers, since patients hitting their out-of-pocket maximum faster means the plan pays more.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: Strong benefit to patients who receive financial help with medical bills, offset by a cost borne by insurers that could be passed through to premiums.

outcome.mechanism: It was introduced in November 2021 and referred to the Energy and Commerce Committee, but never received a vote before Congress adjourned in January 2023.

narrative.text: The bill attracted 62 cosponsors across both parties but was never brought to a House floor vote.

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: Health insurance companies benefit because they avoid the added cost of counting third-party payments toward patient cost-sharing limits.

analysis.who_came_out_ahead_short: Health insurers avoided added cost-sharing mandates

for.name: Rep. A. Donald McEachin
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill and championed it.

for.name: Rep. Rodney Davis
for.what_they_did: Helped introduce the bill with bipartisan support.

sides.party_line_note: Cosponsors split 58 Democrats and 4 Republicans, though the bill never reached a floor vote.

industries.note: Plans would pay more of patient costs as third-party payments count toward deductibles and out-of-pocket limits.
